solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discarded wit of Spooner, one with lots to say

indicators.note: naming Spooner tells the solver to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: something discarded has been binned, thrown in the rubbish bin
a wag is a joker, a wit

explanation.surface: A rejected joke attributed to the famously muddled Oxford don, from someone who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: BINNED WAG with its opening sounds swapped becomes 'winned bag', spelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded talker who goes on and on is called this, an informal insult.

clue.text: Female priest can chat and be funny

indicators.note: something funny is odd or out of order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A priestess who can chatter away and be amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchante was a female follower and priestess of Bacchus, the Roman wine god.

clue.text: Magic when vermouth is put in cocktail

indicators.note: one thing put in another sits inside it, so the vermouth's letters go inside

parts.note: mojo is a magic charm or power
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Something magical happens when vermouth goes into a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a pub order for Italian (sweet) vermouth, as in 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban rum drink with mint and lime is one example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: Is fellow by end of short story a bringer of luck?

indicators.note: placed by the end of means set right after, so these pieces follow
a short word is cut, so the story loses its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man at the close of a brief story brings good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm or amulet is carried because it is believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Abused page started to recover

definitions.meaning: a page mistreated by folding down its corner to mark one's place
began to get better after a crisis or illness

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: a dog-eared page has had its corner turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes passing the critical point of an illness or crisis and beginning to improve.

clue.text: Poet to be very fond of Anglo-Catholic finery?

parts.note: to love is to be very fond of
high-church clergy wear lace on their vestments, such as cottas and albs

explanation.surface: A poet who adores the lacy trimmings of high-church worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Lovelace was a 17th-century Cavalier poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace wrote 'To Althea, from Prison', so he is a named example of a poet.

clue.text: Child accommodated by school's programme

indicators.note: something accommodated by these words is lodged inside them, spanning the join

explanation.surface: A pupil is taken into a school's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a small child or baby.

clue.text: A top article in ancient language

parts.note: a vest is a top, a garment for the upper body
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A leading article written in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures is an ancient language.

clue.text: Rogue depositing one vehicle in river

indicators.note: the river deposits these letters in itself, holding them within

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
I is the Roman numeral one
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A villain dumps a car in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a rascal, hero of the picaresque novel, means a rogue.

clue.text: Returned as Wimbledon champion, glowing outwardly?

indicators.note: glowing on the outside, so those letters wrap round the champion

parts.note: red as in red-hot, glowing
Chris Evert won the Wimbledon singles three times

explanation.surface: Someone came back as the tennis winner, looking radiant.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to go back to an earlier state, so the past tense is a synonym.

clue.text: Bringing out temptation son should avoid

indicators.note: the temptation must steer clear of the son, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: seduction is temptation, enticement

explanation.surface: A moral warning: bringing out temptation is something a son should avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduction is a rare word for the act of drawing out or extracting something.

clue.text: Smooth stars appearing outside entrance briefly

indicators.note: the stars show on the outside, wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: a brief word is clipped, losing its last letter

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Stars glide in briefly through the stage door.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term directs that notes be played smoothly connected, without gaps.

clue.text: Soldier given no identity suffering mental disorder

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
ID is short for identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: A soldier stripped of his identity suffers a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone afflicted by irrational suspicion and delusions of persecution has that mental disorder.

clue.text: Action by angler brings fish after very short time

indicators.note: the fish comes after the short time, so these letters follow

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler's technique lands a fish almost at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Trout can be caught by hand by stroking their bellies, a poacher's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching trout by stroking them underwater until they can be scooped out is a fishing method.

clue.text: Given honour and praise, it's right she from France should be embraced

indicators.note: these letters are hugged by the praise, placed inside it

parts.note: to laud is to praise
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is rightly hugged and praised as she receives an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowned with bay leaves, the ancient symbol of victory, means honoured.

clue.text: Expected to be quiet, tot dumped in grass

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: the tot is dumped inside the grass, so its letters go within

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum

explanation.surface: A toddler is meant to stay silent after being dropped in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' reads as a small child but means a sum added up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something presumed is taken for granted, assumed or expected to be so.

clue.text: Those troubled about getting first in English may be what's found in Oxford?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Anxious people get top marks in English, just as you might find at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges THOSE into SHOET. Oxford is not the university but a laced shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaped wooden form slipped into a shoe to keep it in shape sits inside an Oxford brogue.

clue.text: One's cast out at sea — gets to talk endlessly about nothing

indicators.note: the endless talk goes about, round, the nothing

parts.note: to harp on is to talk about something endlessly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sailor lost overboard keeps rambling on about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed spear thrown at whales from a ship is cast out at sea.

clue.text: Like some performances for men only — I will stay outside

indicators.note: the I stays on the outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a stag party or night is for men only

explanation.surface: A man barred from a men-only show says he'll wait outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Performances that happen in front of an audience in a theatre are described this way.

clue.text: Jumping around, being concerned to make space for exercise

indicators.note: the caring makes room for the exercise, taking it inside

parts.note: caring is being concerned
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone bounding about out of concern to clear room for a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or leap about playfully, so the participle means jumping around.

clue.text: Each year idol is placed atop a temple

indicators.note: in a down clue placed atop means written above, so these letters come first

parts.note: pa is short for per annum, each year
an idol is a god

explanation.surface: Every year a statue of a deity is set on top of a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine is a kind of temple.

clue.text: Female is very admirable in party attire?

parts.note: slang 'rocks', as in 'she rocks', means is excellent

explanation.surface: A woman looks wonderful in her party outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresses are worn to parties; the query flags that they are only one kind of attire.

clue.text: Story of a former Chelsea manager

definitions.meaning: a short tale, the French term used for a short story
Antonio ... managed Chelsea football club from 2016 to 2018

explanation.definitionFit: A short literary tale is called by this French word; Antonio Conte was Chelsea's Italian manager.

clue.text: What Queen embodies is good in truth

indicators.note: the good goes in the truth, inside its letters

parts.note: reality is truth, what actually is

explanation.surface: The monarch personifies goodness in truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal status or kingly dignity is what a monarch embodies.

clue.text: Name of unimportant person in organisation with sexist message?

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor figure in a big organisation
a sign reading 'no men' excludes one sex

explanation.surface: Asks what to call a lowly employee in a firm sending out discriminatory notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a surname or nickname, originally the third Roman name.

clue.text: Search taking road back to border

indicators.note: going back means these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A hunt that follows a road back to the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a river is to drag its bed, searching for something lost.

clue.text: One with plan to be kind, not out to be first

indicators.note: the not-out piece comes first, so its letters lead

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is not out is in
tender means kind, gentle

explanation.surface: Someone who means to be kind and is keen not to finish last.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket batsmen still at the crease are 'in', not out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who intends something, who has a purpose in mind, holds a plan.
